title: Public sector accessibility (EU)
description: Questions for the accessibility and bid owners and repository checks for websites and mobile applications delivered to EU public sector bodies under Directive (EU) 2016/2102, tested against EN 301 549 V3.2.1, the harmonised standard that Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/1339 references, and for contracts awarded under Directive 2014/24/EU. Covers EU law only; national transpositions such as France's RGAA add their own requirements. These rules do not establish compliance.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2016/2102 on the accessibility of the websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies
Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/1339, harmonised standard EN 301 549 V3.2.1 for Directive (EU) 2016/2102
ETSI EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (2021-03), Accessibility requirements for ICT products and services

rules.instruction: Ask the bid owner which accessibility criteria the contracting authority set in the technical specifications of the contract (Directive 2014/24/EU Art. 42(1)), and record them with the change.
rules.verification: Link the recorded criteria and the contract clause they come from.

rules.instruction: Test each changed web page against EN 301 549 V3.2.1 clause 9 (Web), including the conformance requirements of clause 9.6.
rules.verification: Link the test report that lists each failed requirement with its fix or its open issue.

rules.instruction: For a changed mobile or desktop application, test the changed screens against EN 301 549 V3.2.1 clause 11 (Software).
rules.verification: Link the test report for the changed screens.

rules.instruction: When the change adds user documentation or a support channel, apply EN 301 549 V3.2.1 clause 12 (Documentation and support services) to it.
rules.verification: Check the new documentation and support pages against clause 12 and link the result.

rules.instruction: Ask the public body's accessibility owner to update the accessibility statement when the change adds, removes or fixes content that is not accessible (Directive (EU) 2016/2102 Art. 7(1)).
rules.verification: Open the statement and check that its date and its list of content that is not accessible follow the release.

rules.instruction: Keep the feedback mechanism of Directive (EU) 2016/2102 Art. 7(1)(b) reachable from the changed pages, so that users can report a failure and ask for content that is not accessible.
rules.verification: Open a changed page and follow its link to the feedback mechanism.

rules.instruction: When content stays not accessible, ask the public body's owner whether they claim a disproportionate burden under Art. 5 of Directive (EU) 2016/2102, and record their assessment; the team does not decide it.
rules.verification: Link the owner's recorded assessment from the change.
